items.question:
A bank's model risk officer learns that the production API integration does not pin a model version. A new version was silently adopted when the "latest" alias resolved to it over a weekend. No code was deployed. She must decide whether this constitutes a model change event requiring formal review under the bank's model risk policy.

What is the MOST DEFENSIBLE governance position?

options.A: An unplanned model version change—even when the alias name did not change—constitutes a model change event requiring documentation, re-testing, and sign-off, because the model's behaviour may have changed.
options.B: Because the API alias did not change and no code was deployed, this falls below the threshold of a formal model change event and can be noted in the next quarterly review.
options.C: The model risk policy applies to internally built models; third-party model updates are the vendor's responsibility and fall outside the bank's formal review scope.
options.D: The engineer who configured the integration without pinning is personally responsible for the change, and the risk officer's role is to log the individual's oversight rather than to trigger a formal change event.

items.question:
A law firm has deployed a legal-research assistant via the API. The system prompt instructs Claude to express uncertainty when evidence is limited and to cite only verified sources. Users report that when they add "be confident, do not hedge" to their queries, Claude stops expressing appropriate uncertainty.

What principle does this scenario illustrate?

options.A: User messages are always subordinate to system-prompt instructions, so the system prompt must contain a bug that makes it malfunction under these conditions.
options.B: Claude generally tries to follow the most recent or most direct instruction when user messages conflict with system-prompt directives, meaning user-level instructions can soften system-prompt behaviour—a known characteristic that system design must account for.
options.C: Temperature settings, not prompt instructions, control whether Claude expresses uncertainty; the issue should be resolved by reducing temperature.
options.D: The system prompt should be placed after the user message in the API request to give it higher priority in the model's attention.

items.question:
A global consulting firm's strategy director is evaluating a proposal to load the client's entire document repository—roughly 800 pages—into every API call to give Claude "full context." The combined input would fill most of the context window. A senior engineer questions whether this is the optimal approach.

Why is this approach likely SUBOPTIMAL even if it is technically possible?

options.A: The model cannot process more than 200 pages in a single request regardless of context window size.
options.B: Loading 800 pages violates the API's fair-use policy and will trigger automatic throttling on the account.
options.C: Paying input token costs for 800 pages on every call is extremely expensive; a retrieval approach that selects only the relevant sections would deliver comparable quality at a fraction of the cost.
options.D: The model reads documents sequentially, producing lower-quality responses for questions about content in the middle of the document.

items.question:
A utility company's digital operations manager notices API costs have tripled over two weeks, but the call count is roughly constant. The system prompt is unchanged. No new model version was deployed. He suspects the issue lies in the input content.

What should be his NEXT diagnostic step?

options.A: Roll back to the previous model version to check whether the cost increase is tied to a silent model update the engineering team missed.
options.B: Audit the system prompt for accidental duplication of sections that may have been introduced by a recent copy-paste error.
options.C: Enable verbose logging and sample 20 calls to examine output token counts and determine whether responses have become longer.
options.D: Compare the average input token count per call over the last two weeks against the prior period to determine whether input payloads have grown—for example, longer documents or additional history being passed in.

items.question:
A media company's creative director uses a Claude API integration for brainstorming campaign ideas. Since a recent configuration change set temperature to 0.05, every brainstorming session produces nearly identical idea lists.

What does this scenario illustrate about the appropriate use of low temperature settings?

options.A: Low temperature trades creativity and variety for consistency and determinism—desirable for classification and extraction tasks but counterproductive for creative ideation where output diversity is the goal.
options.B: Temperature 0.05 is slightly too low; setting it to exactly 0.00 would restore variability by engaging a different sampling mechanism.
options.C: The creative director should switch to a higher-tier model, which maintains creative diversity even at low temperature settings.
options.D: Adding a "be creative and varied" instruction to the system prompt overrides the temperature setting and restores output diversity.

items.question:
A startup consultancy's principal consultant builds an API-based meeting-assistant that keeps full conversation history in each session. After about 90 minutes of a meeting, clients report shorter, less detailed responses and occasional apparent lapses in memory of earlier points.

What is the MOST LIKELY technical cause?

options.A: The model detects extended session lengths and applies latency-optimisation measures that reduce output quality.
options.B: As conversation history accumulates, the growing input token count pushes the session toward the context window limit, leaving less token budget for the model to generate thorough responses.
options.C: The API rate limit resets after a certain number of tokens in a session, causing temporary throttling that shortens output length.
options.D: After a long session, the model's effective temperature rises, causing less-focused and more abbreviated responses.

items.question:
A retailer's merchandising director is told by IT that their new Claude API integration requires an "API key." She asks what this means in plain business terms.

What is the MOST accurate description of an API key?

options.A: A password that individual employees use to log into the Claude.ai interface, separate from their corporate SSO credentials.
options.B: A billing plan identifier that determines which model tier the organisation has access to.
options.C: A credential that authenticates the organisation's software application to the Claude API, enabling it to make authorised requests and ensuring usage is tracked to the correct account.
options.D: A configuration file that stores the system prompt and temperature settings for a specific integration.

items.question:
A financial services firm's operations analyst generates standardised trade-confirmation letters using Claude.ai. Different team members produce slightly different letter formats because they phrase prompts differently. A quality manager asks whether the API could resolve this inconsistency.

What API capability would MOST directly address the format inconsistency?

options.A: The API's higher rate limit allows more letters to be generated simultaneously, reducing pressure on individual team members to rush their prompts.
options.B: The API enforces stricter content-safety filtering that prevents off-format outputs from being returned to users.
options.C: The API gives access to a model tier fine-tuned specifically for financial document generation.
options.D: The API allows a developer to set a fixed system prompt and low temperature that every request runs against, removing individual variation in how team members phrase the task.

items.question:
An operations excellence manager at a 50,000-employee manufacturer is evaluating which of two Claude use cases should migrate from Claude.ai to the API. Use Case 1: A daily automated quality-defect report sent before the 6 AM shift. Use Case 2: An analyst who occasionally asks Claude to help draft emails.

Which TWO characteristics of Use Case 1 distinguish it as the correct API migration candidate? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The defect report is more strategically important than the analyst's email drafting, so it deserves a more robust technical solution.
options.B: The report must run at a fixed time without human intervention, which the chat interface cannot support.
options.C: The defect report contains sensitive operational data that should not flow through a consumer product.
options.D: The same structured query is sent every day with only the defect data changing, making it a repeatable, automatable task.
options.E: The production floor team lacks Claude.ai accounts, so the API is the only way to deliver the report to them.

items.question:
A hospital's VP of technology is reviewing a proposal to use the API for real-time clinical decision support during patient triage. The API tier's rate limit can handle 95% of projected peak load. The risk committee asks what the 5% overflow scenario means for patient care.

What is the MOST IMPORTANT concern the VP should raise with the engineering team?

options.A: A rate-limit error during real-time clinical decision support could cause a recommendation to fail at a critical moment; the architecture must define a safe fallback that preserves patient safety when the API is throttled.
options.B: A 5% overflow rate is within industry-standard API availability targets and does not require special engineering attention beyond what is already planned.
options.C: The engineering team should request a higher rate limit from the provider, and the risk committee should approve the budget for a tier upgrade before go-live.
options.D: The system should log throttled events and allow a clinician to manually re-submit the request, which is the standard pattern for rate-limit handling in clinical IT.

items.question:
A consulting firm's engagement director has delivered an AI-augmented analysis workflow to a client. The client's legal team asks whether the AI model is "stable" and whether future changes will affect the deliverables. She must respond accurately.

What is the MOST COMPLETE and ACCURATE statement she can make?

options.A: "The model provider guarantees stability within a named model version, so as long as the version name doesn't change, the output will be identical."
options.B: "We have pinned the integration to a specific model version, meaning the model's behaviour won't change unless we explicitly perform a documented upgrade; any future version change will be treated as a project change event."
options.C: "AI model outputs are inherently variable and cannot be guaranteed consistent even within a pinned version, so the client should treat each output as a fresh result requiring full re-verification."
options.D: "The model provider continuously improves the model, so the version in use today will automatically improve over time without any action from our team."

items.question:
A law firm's contract manager is surprised that a Claude API call analysing a 40-page contract and returning a one-paragraph summary costs nearly as much as calls generating multi-page outputs.

Which explanation BEST accounts for this?

options.A: Summary tasks require more reasoning steps than generation tasks, which drives up compute cost even when output is brief.
options.B: Short outputs are billed at a premium per-token rate because they require the model to compress information more intensively.
options.C: The cost reflects the large volume of input tokens consumed by the 40-page contract; input costs are substantial even when the output is brief.
options.D: The API charges a flat per-call fee plus a small variable component, so call count—not token count—drives the cost.

items.question:
A telecoms company's head of digital wants to embed a Claude-powered troubleshooting guide into 5 million customers' mobile apps. She asks her architecture team whether Claude.ai or the API is the right foundation.

Which consideration is DECISIVE in choosing the API?

options.A: The API provides dedicated compute so 5 million simultaneous users won't experience latency caused by shared Claude.ai infrastructure.
options.B: The API allows the company to use a custom model fine-tuned on their specific network equipment documentation.
options.C: The API is GDPR-compliant while Claude.ai is not, making it the only option for a consumer-facing product in Europe.
options.D: Embedding AI functionality inside the telecoms company's own app requires programmatic API access; Claude.ai is a consumer product that cannot be white-labelled or called by application code.

items.question:
A bank's head of operations is briefing the executive team on an API integration the technology team has built. Two colleagues ask about "temperature" and "system prompt."

Which TWO descriptions accurately represent these parameters to a non-technical audience? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The system prompt is a set of standing instructions the application sends to Claude before every user interaction, establishing the assistant's role, scope, and behavioural guardrails.
options.B: Temperature is a safety control that prevents Claude from producing regulated financial advice regardless of how users phrase their questions.
options.C: Temperature is a dial between consistency and creativity: set low, Claude produces predictable, stable outputs for compliance-sensitive tasks; set high, it explores a wider range of phrasings and ideas.
options.D: The system prompt is a hidden password layer that prevents Claude from revealing to users that the tool is AI-powered.
options.E: Temperature controls response speed: higher temperature produces faster but lower-quality outputs; lower temperature produces slower but more accurate outputs.

items.question:
An insurer's chief digital officer is reviewing a proposal to build a real-time API pipeline that sends each customer's full claim history—averaging 45 pages—to Claude during a live agent call. The system must respond within 8 seconds. The engineering team flags concerns about context window size, output latency, and token cost simultaneously.

What is the SINGLE MOST ACTIONABLE recommendation the CDO should bring back to the engineering team?

options.A: Rather than loading the full 45-page history on every call, implement a retrieval layer that extracts the 5–10 most relevant pages for each query, dramatically reducing context size, latency, and cost while keeping the 8-second target achievable.
options.B: Upgrade to the highest-tier model, which has a larger context window and lower latency at any input size, resolving all three concerns simultaneously.
options.C: Pre-summarise each customer's claim history into a single 2-page profile and replace the rolling 45-page input, accepting that historical nuance will be lost.
options.D: Extend the SLA from 8 seconds to 20 seconds to give the model adequate processing time for the full 45-page document load.

items.question:
A federal agency's AI program manager oversees a Claude API integration used for benefits-eligibility determinations affecting thousands of applicants. The engineering team has been updating the system prompt informally as policy guidance changes, without documentation or sign-off from the policy team.

What is the PRIMARY governance risk this practice creates?

options.A: Informal prompt changes risk introducing token sequences that exceed the context window and cause silent API errors.
options.B: If system prompt changes affect eligibility outputs but are undocumented, the agency cannot demonstrate that the AI behaved consistently with its governing policy at any point in time—a significant accountability and audit risk.
options.C: The policy team losing visibility over prompt changes increases the risk that Claude adopts a persona inconsistent with the agency's communication standards.
options.D: Informal prompt changes mean the integration will fail when the model version is eventually upgraded, because the new version won't have been tested with the revised system prompt.

items.question:
A mid-size utility's data science manager is planning a six-month API-based energy-usage analysis programme. Volume will be light for the first two months, then ramp to peak load by month four. She asks whether to request a high-rate API tier from the start.

Which consideration is MOST important in deciding when to upgrade the API tier?

options.A: Starting on the highest tier immediately eliminates any risk of disruption during the ramp-up phase, regardless of the extra cost during low-traffic months.
options.B: API tier contracts cannot be changed after initial commitment, so it is always safest to begin at the highest tier available.
options.C: Understanding the traffic ramp profile and timing the tier upgrade to coincide with the volume increase balances cost efficiency during testing with capacity readiness for peak load.
options.D: Rate limits are not enforced for batch analytical workloads, only for real-time interactive applications, so tier selection does not affect this use case.

items.question:
A management consulting firm's senior associate builds an API research assistant that appends the full conversation history to every new request. After two weeks of use, API costs are unexpectedly high despite a constant number of user questions per day.

What is the MOST LIKELY cause?

options.A: The API is billing for the same conversation history multiple times due to a known concurrency bug in the session-management library.
options.B: The number of output tokens per response has grown as the model generates longer answers over time for mature conversations.
options.C: The model performs additional "thinking" passes over the growing history on each call, increasing compute cost without increasing billed tokens.
options.D: As conversation history grows, the input token count per call increases because the entire accumulated history is re-sent with each new request, compounding cost over time.

items.question:
A pharma company's head of regulatory operations is troubleshooting an API integration for regulatory submission summaries. Users report two problems: costs have risen sharply, and summaries occasionally omit required sections. The model version has not changed. The system prompt was recently edited independently by two team members without version control.

What is the FIRST diagnostic step she should take?

options.A: Retrieve and compare the current system prompt against the last known-good version to identify whether the independent edits introduced conflicting instructions or removed critical guidance governing which sections to include.
options.B: Run the integration with a minimal system prompt to see whether the quality issue resolves, confirming the system prompt is the root cause.
options.C: Audit the average input token count per call over the past two weeks to determine whether cost is being driven by larger inputs.
options.D: Ask Claude to critique its most recent output against the required section list to self-identify any omissions.

items.question:
A law firm's discovery manager is using an API integration for document review that maintains a full conversation history per case. For a large case, the integration produces degraded responses after about three hours. The team asks whether to increase context window allocation, switch to a higher-tier model, or restructure conversation management.

What should the manager recommend?

options.A: Switching to a higher-tier model is correct because higher-tier models handle longer conversation histories with better quality.
options.B: The underlying issue is growing conversation history consuming most of the context window; the correct fix is to periodically summarise and compress earlier turns rather than simply buying more capacity.
options.C: Increasing the context window allocation directly resolves the issue by providing more space for the growing conversation history.
options.D: Each document should be reviewed in a separate API call with no shared conversation state, eliminating the quality issue entirely.

items.question:
A bank's technology risk manager is reviewing an API integration for automated fraud-alert narratives. The system prompt instructs Claude to summarise flagged transactions consistently. The temperature is set to 0.8. The risk committee flags that identical fraud patterns produce narratives with significantly different urgency levels across cases.

Which adjustment would MOST directly resolve the inconsistency while preserving the system's utility?

options.A: Strengthen the system prompt instructions to explicitly prohibit varying urgency language, which will override the high temperature effect.
options.B: Replace the current model with a lower-tier model, which has less inherent variability in its outputs at the same temperature.
options.C: Reduce temperature to a low value so that structurally similar cases consistently produce similar narratives, addressing the root cause of urgency variability.
options.D: Post-process all narratives with a rule-based classifier that normalises urgency to three standard levels before delivery to the risk committee.

items.question:
An insurer's AI governance officer is implementing a framework requiring all API integrations to pin specific model versions. One engineering team raises two legitimate objections to strict version pinning.

Which TWO objections represent genuine trade-offs of strict version pinning? (Choose TWO)

options.A: A pinned integration will not automatically benefit from bug fixes or safety improvements in newer model versions, requiring deliberate upgrades to receive those improvements.
options.B: Version pinning requires more mature change-management processes—testing, documentation, sign-off for each upgrade—which increases engineering overhead compared to tracking the latest alias.
options.C: Pinning a version prevents the team from increasing the context window size for individual API requests, limiting how much input data can be sent.
options.D: Pinned model versions carry higher per-token API costs than the latest model version, making high-volume integrations progressively more expensive over time.
options.E: A pinned model version will stop working when the next version is released, because providers retire old versions immediately upon releasing new ones.

items.question:
A bank's head of compliance communications needs to generate thousands of personalised regulatory disclosure letters for different account holders, inserting customer-specific data into a standard template. She is evaluating whether to use Claude.ai with a team of writers or to build an API pipeline.

What is the STRONGEST argument for the API pipeline in this regulated context?

options.A: The API pipeline can generate all letters faster, completing the job in hours rather than days.
options.B: The API ensures letters meet GDPR requirements by routing them through Anthropic's regulatory data-processing agreements.
options.C: The API pipeline allows unlimited simultaneous letter generation, which would exhaust the team's Claude.ai plan limits.
options.D: The API allows the system prompt and temperature to be fixed centrally, guaranteeing every letter follows identical instructions and producing consistent, auditable output at scale.

items.question:
A global manufacturer's digital transformation director is preparing a board briefing on when to use the API versus when Claude.ai is sufficient. She wants a concise decision framework.

Which THREE conditions, if ALL are present, most strongly indicate that the API is required rather than Claude.ai? (Choose THREE)

options.A: The use case involves documents that contain commercially sensitive product data.
options.B: The team expects to use Claude occasionally, fewer than 20 times per week.
options.C: The workflow must run automatically on a defined trigger without a human initiating each request.
options.D: The Claude output must be programmatically written into another business system rather than read by a human.
options.E: The same structured prompt will be sent at high volume with only the variable data changing across each call.

items.question:
An operations manager at a 400-person logistics firm wants Claude to generate a shipment delay report by pulling current status data from the company's tracking system. Her analysts currently copy-paste data into a chat window before asking questions. She asks the IT team whether a more direct integration exists.

Which capability BEST addresses this need?

options.A: Tool use, which lets Claude call an external system at inference time and incorporate the returned data into its response.
options.B: Prompt caching, which stores the system prompt so repeated queries run faster and cheaper.
options.C: Batch processing, which queues multiple prompts for asynchronous execution overnight.
options.D: A fine-tuned model, which learns the firm's data schema and retrieves live records without external calls.

items.question:
An IT director at a 1,200-person insurance company is evaluating how to give multiple Claude-powered workflows access to the policy management system, claims database, and document repository. Her team built one custom integration for the policy system and found the development and maintenance cost high. She wants to know whether a standardised approach exists.

The capability she is looking for is BEST described as:

options.A: Prompt chaining, which connects multiple Claude calls in sequence to access different data sources.
options.B: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides a standardised interface for connecting Claude to external tools and data systems.
options.C: A shared Project knowledge base, where all system data is uploaded once and referenced across sessions.
options.D: Extended thinking, which allows Claude to reason over complex queries without requiring external data access.

items.question:
A digital transformation lead at a retail bank is evaluating two proposed Claude implementations. The first drafts a one-page credit risk summary each time an analyst uploads a PDF. The second autonomously monitors a shared inbox, classifies each incoming email, routes it to the correct team, drafts an initial response, and flags anomalies for human review.

Which statement BEST explains why the second implementation requires an agent architecture?

options.A: The second task is too complex for a single context window, requiring the work to be split across multiple model instances.
options.B: Agent architectures reduce hallucination risk because the model checks each step against a predefined rule set before proceeding.
options.C: The second task requires multiple sequential decisions, tool invocations, and branching logic that cannot be fully encoded in a single prompt-response exchange.
options.D: Single-shot prompts are limited to text inputs; only agents can process email attachments and structured metadata.

items.question: A senior consultant is advising a pharmaceutical company on which Claude-powered workflows should use agent architectures versus single-shot implementations. The company proposes five workflows. Which TWO characteristics MOST strongly justify an agent design? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The workflow queries a live clinical trial database, evaluates the returned data, and then decides which of three downstream systems to update based on the result.
options.B: The workflow processes a high volume of short, structurally identical requests that follow the same pattern every time.
options.C: The workflow drafts a regulatory document, submits it to a review API, interprets the feedback, and revises the draft before finalising.
options.D: The workflow converts supplier invoice PDFs into structured records using a fixed extraction template.
options.E: The workflow summarises a 60-page submission into a two-page executive briefing.

items.question:
A knowledge management lead at a global pharmaceutical company is designing a system to help scientists query the company's 50,000-document research library. An internal debate has emerged between loading all relevant documents into a very long context window per query, versus implementing a retrieval system that fetches only the most relevant documents first.

The PRIMARY advantage of the retrieval approach at this scale is:

options.A: Retrieval eliminates hallucination risk because retrieved documents are always factually accurate before being passed to Claude.
options.B: Long-context windows degrade response quality when documents use technical or scientific language.
options.C: Retrieval is always faster because smaller inputs process in less time regardless of infrastructure.
options.D: Loading 50,000 documents into a single context window is not feasible; retrieval narrows the input to what is relevant, making the query tractable and controlling cost.

items.question:
An analytics lead at a 30-person non-profit wants Claude to generate individual impact reports for each of the organisation's 2,400 donors. The reports do not need to be delivered in real time — the organisation sends its annual report pack in a scheduled overnight batch. The lead's primary concern is cost.

Which capability BEST fits this scenario?

options.A: Batch processing, which queues multiple prompts for asynchronous execution at a reduced per-request cost.
options.B: Prompt caching, which stores common prompt sections and reduces cost on repeated identical contexts.
options.C: A multi-agent pipeline, which distributes the 2,400 reports across parallel agent instances for faster delivery.
options.D: Extended thinking, which produces more thorough outputs per request and reduces the need for human editing.

items.question:
A product manager at a 200-person SaaS company has built a Claude-powered customer support assistant. The system prompt is 3,000 tokens long and describes product features, pricing tiers, known issues, and response style guidelines. The company receives roughly 8,000 customer inquiries per day; each call includes the full system prompt plus the customer's message. The team is reviewing the API bill and wants to reduce input token costs.

Which statement BEST describes why prompt caching is worth evaluating?

options.A: Prompt caching automatically removes redundant sentences from the system prompt, shortening it on future requests.
options.B: The system prompt is long, identical across all 8,000 daily requests, and represents the dominant share of input tokens — caching it would substantially reduce the per-request input token cost.
options.C: Prompt caching compresses the system prompt into a smaller token representation, freeing up context window space for longer customer messages.
options.D: Prompt caching learns from previous customer interactions and progressively improves the quality of the system prompt guidelines.

items.question:
An L&D manager at a 45,000-person manufacturing firm wants Claude to generate training materials in a consistent house style: specific machinery terminology, a defined reading level, and a particular document structure. Her team proposes fine-tuning a model to embed the house style. A colleague argues that a well-designed system prompt with a few illustrative examples could achieve the same result without fine-tuning.

In this scenario, the colleague's position is MOST defensible because:

options.A: Fine-tuning permanently modifies the base model and cannot be updated when house style guidelines change.
options.B: Fine-tuning is only available for entry-tier models that lack the reasoning depth needed for complex training materials.
options.C: For style and format consistency, context engineering — explicit guidelines and representative examples in the system prompt — is typically the right first lever, with fine-tuning reserved for when context alone consistently fails.
options.D: System prompts and examples are free of engineering cost, whereas fine-tuning requires purchasing dedicated hardware.

items.question:
A solutions architect at a telecoms company has deployed a Claude-powered assistant that uses tool calling to query a customer account database. During testing, the team observes that when the database returns a record with a missing field — for example, a contract renewal date that is null — Claude sometimes generates a plausible-looking date rather than surfacing the gap to the user.

This behaviour MOST directly illustrates which failure mode?

options.A: Rate limiting, where the tool is called too frequently and the system returns degraded data to prevent overload.
options.B: Prompt injection, where a malicious value in the returned record manipulates Claude's subsequent instructions.
options.C: Context window overflow, where the tool result is truncated before Claude can read the full record.
options.D: Claude treating the tool output as a grounding source while still applying parametric text generation to fill gaps within that output.

items.question: A chief of staff at a 3,000-bed hospital network is evaluating two architecture proposals for a Claude-powered clinical reference assistant: one uses RAG over the clinical guidelines corpus; the other loads full guidelines into a long context window per query. Which TWO statements accurately characterise trade-offs she should weigh? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Long context windows guarantee higher factual accuracy than retrieval because the model sees all material simultaneously.
options.B: RAG risks returning an incomplete answer if the retrieval step fails to surface the most relevant guideline passage.
options.C: Long context is always cheaper than RAG because retrieval infrastructure costs offset any token savings.
options.D: Long context becomes cost-prohibitive and operationally impractical when the corpus is large enough that no single context window can hold it.
options.E: RAG eliminates hallucination because retrieved documents are passed verbatim into context without modification.

items.question:
A process automation lead at a mid-size energy company is reviewing four proposed Claude-powered workflows. Her engineering team recommends agent architectures for all four. She suspects some should be single-shot implementations instead.

Which workflow does NOT warrant an agent architecture?

options.A: Monitoring a regulatory filing inbox, extracting key deadlines, cross-referencing them against the compliance calendar, and updating a shared tracker.
options.B: Generating a weekly safety compliance summary from a pre-formatted structured data export that follows the same schema every week.
options.C: Drafting a response to a regulator inquiry, submitting it to a legal review API, incorporating the review feedback, and preparing a revised draft.
options.D: Triaging maintenance work orders: classifying severity, looking up parts availability in a live inventory system, and routing to the correct team queue.

items.question:
An AI program manager at a global bank deployed a Claude-powered loan documentation assistant six months ago. The compliance team now raises a concern: output quality may have drifted since a prompt update three months ago, but no one can confirm this because no baseline measurements were taken at launch.

Which statement BEST describes what an evals practice would have provided?

options.A: Evals would have prevented the prompt update from deploying until all output quality metrics exceeded a minimum threshold.
options.B: Evals would have automatically flagged the quality drift and rolled back the prompt to its original version.
options.C: Evals would have established measurable output quality baselines at launch, enabling a structured comparison against current outputs to confirm or rule out drift.
options.D: Evals would have generated synthetic test cases continuously, replacing the need for human review of live outputs.

items.question:
A content strategist at a large media company uses Claude via the API to generate article variants. Her system prompt includes 2,500 words of brand guidelines, editorial style rules, and audience personas. She notices per-request costs are higher than expected and asks her developer to investigate. The developer says prompt caching would reduce costs.

The PRIMARY reason caching would help is:

options.A: Prompt caching automatically selects which requests share enough context to batch them together for a volume discount.
options.B: Prompt caching encrypts repeated system prompts, reducing the token count that the billing system measures.
options.C: Prompt caching reduces latency on the first request by pre-loading the system prompt before any user query is sent.
options.D: Prompt caching stores the processed version of the repeated system prompt so subsequent requests pay a lower cost for that portion rather than re-processing it as fresh input tokens each time.

items.question: The head of AI at a 600-store retail chain is evaluating fine-tuning versus context engineering for a product recommendation assistant. The assistant must use the chain's promotional pricing rules, specific category taxonomy labels, and a casual conversational register. Which TWO statements ACCURATELY describe considerations that should inform this decision? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Fine-tuning is the only reliable way to enforce specific terminology and taxonomy; system prompts cannot consistently reproduce precise labelling conventions.
options.B: Context engineering is inappropriate when the system prompt exceeds 500 tokens because longer prompts introduce unacceptable latency.
options.C: Fine-tuning requires a curated training dataset and ongoing maintenance as promotional rules change — this overhead should be weighed against prompt-based solutions that can be updated immediately.
options.D: Fine-tuning permanently prevents the model from following instructions not covered by the training data, limiting future use cases on the same model.
options.E: Context engineering — an explicit system prompt with taxonomy rules, a few illustrative examples, and format instructions — is typically the right first lever before investing in fine-tuning.

items.question:
A project manager at a government agency has deployed Claude to assist with drafting public communications. A senior manager asks how the team will know whether Claude's output quality consistently meets the agency's plain-language and accuracy standards over time.

The MOST appropriate mechanism to ensure ongoing quality visibility is:

options.A: A set of representative test inputs with defined quality criteria, run periodically against the live deployment to measure whether outputs continue to meet the standard.
options.B: Requiring a different team member to review every output each week so that fresh eyes catch any drift in quality.
options.C: Upgrading to a higher-tier model, which produces more reliable output and reduces the need for structured quality measurement.
options.D: Adding a sentence to the system prompt asking Claude to self-report any response where it is uncertain about plain-language compliance.

items.question:
An enterprise architect at a logistics conglomerate is evaluating how to give its new Claude-powered operations dashboard access to five internal systems: a route planning API, a warehouse management system, a carrier performance database, a customs documentation platform, and a real-time GPS feed. One engineer recommends bespoke Claude integrations for each system; another recommends MCP servers.

The STRONGEST argument for the MCP-based approach is:

options.A: MCP servers auto-discover available endpoints in each system and configure themselves without engineering effort.
options.B: Bespoke integrations are not supported for enterprise Claude accounts, making MCP the only available option.
options.C: MCP provides a standardised interface layer — each additional system requires a server implementation rather than bespoke Claude-integration code — making the integration estate easier to maintain and extend.
options.D: MCP servers are maintained by Anthropic and updated automatically when Claude's capabilities change, reducing long-term ownership cost.

items.question:
A financial services firm has deployed a Claude agent that uses tool calling to pull account data, calculate a risk score, and populate a compliance report. The team discovers that when the risk tool returns a score of exactly 70 on a 0–100 scale — the boundary between two risk tiers — Claude inconsistently routes the case to different tiers across otherwise identical inputs. The tool itself is deterministic and returns exactly 70 in all test cases.

The MOST likely root cause is:

options.A: The boundary value triggers a rate limit in the API, causing the model to default to a conservative tier on throttled requests.
options.B: Claude's generation is non-deterministic by default; without an explicit decision rule in the system prompt, boundary cases are resolved by probabilistic text generation rather than deterministic logic.
options.C: Boundary values in tool outputs are not transmitted correctly; the protocol rounds values to the nearest integer, introducing variance.
options.D: The risk scoring tool is stateful and caches previous routing decisions, causing earlier calls to influence later tier assignments.

items.question: A data operations manager at an insurance firm is evaluating which workflows are good candidates for Claude's batch processing mode. Which TWO of the following are BEST suited for batch processing? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Generating individual coverage gap summaries for 15,000 commercial policy renewals due within the next 30 days.
options.B: Answering a broker's live question about a specific policyholder's coverage exclusions during a client call.
options.C: Running sentiment analysis on 8,000 customer complaint emails received during the previous quarter.
options.D: Providing a real-time pre-binding risk assessment that underwriters need within 30 seconds of uploading a new application.
options.E: Generating a one-time strategic briefing for the CEO on emerging cyber risk trends from a provided market report.

items.question:
A large law firm has deployed a RAG-based research assistant that retrieves passages from its case law database and generates legal memos. Associates report that the assistant occasionally cites case holdings accurately but omits critical qualifying language — for example, stating a general rule without noting that it applies only within a specific jurisdiction or only to a narrow fact pattern.

This failure mode is MOST accurately attributed to:

options.A: The retrieval system returning outdated case summaries that predate subsequent limiting decisions by later courts.
options.B: Claude hallucinating jurisdictional qualifiers that do not exist in the source material.
options.C: Context window constraints that prevent Claude from seeing both the retrieved passage and the memo template simultaneously.
options.D: Retrieval chunking splitting a case's main holding from its qualifying language into separate chunks, so Claude receives the rule but not the qualification.

items.question:
A senior consultant is helping a mid-market logistics company design its first Claude-powered agent. The agent will monitor a freight exception inbox, classify each exception by type, look up the relevant shipment record, and generate a recommended resolution. The team has defined exception types, built a working system prompt, and confirmed API access to the shipment database tool. They are now preparing to move toward deployment.

What should the team do NEXT?

options.A: Run the agent against a curated set of representative test exceptions — including edge cases and ambiguous inputs — to verify classification accuracy and tool call behaviour before deployment.
options.B: Deploy immediately to the full exception inbox and monitor production traffic for failures over the first two weeks.
options.C: Switch to a higher-tier model to ensure the agent handles edge cases reliably, then proceed directly to deployment.
options.D: Submit the system prompt to the compliance team for review before any testing begins.

items.question:
A strategy analyst at a consulting firm needs Claude to summarise a 90-page competitor market report she has as a PDF. A colleague suggests building a tool-use integration to pull reports automatically from the firm's document management system. The analyst only needs this specific summary once.

Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Upload the PDF directly as a file attachment; tool use adds integration overhead that is unnecessary for a one-time or infrequent retrieval task.
options.B: Build the tool-use integration because it caches the document for future reuse across the team.
options.C: Invoke extended thinking mode because large PDF summarisation requires special internal reasoning beyond standard generation.
options.D: Build the integration regardless, because Claude cannot process large documents without a tool-use connection to a document management system.

items.question:
A CTO at a 15-person startup wants Claude to query the company's single CRM system to generate weekly pipeline summaries. An engineer proposes setting up an MCP server for the integration. The CTO is not planning to connect any additional systems in the near term.

The MOST appropriate approach is:

options.A: MCP is required for any integration involving live business systems; direct tool use is only permitted for read-only file operations.
options.B: For a single-system integration with no plans to add more systems, bespoke tool use is simpler than MCP overhead; MCP's advantage materialises when standardising across multiple systems.
options.C: Direct tool use integrations have a weaker security posture than MCP connections and should be avoided when CRM data is involved.
options.D: MCP server setup is largely automated and requires minimal engineering effort regardless of the number of systems involved.

items.question:
A digital product manager at a fintech is designing a three-step analysis pipeline: Step 1 extracts transaction fields from a raw data file. Step 2 calculates risk metrics from the extracted fields. Step 3 formats the metrics into a compliance summary. Each step's output is fully determined by the previous step with no conditional branching or external tool calls needed. The manager asks whether this pipeline needs an agent architecture.

Which statement BEST describes the appropriate design?

options.A: This pipeline needs an agent because it involves three separate Claude calls that must coordinate and pass state between them.
options.B: This pipeline needs an agent because multi-step financial analysis requires iterative validation at each step before proceeding.
options.C: A prompt chain — three sequential Claude calls where each receives the previous step's output as input — is sufficient; agent architecture adds complexity that is only justified when intermediate results require conditional decisions or tool-triggered actions.
options.D: This pipeline requires fine-tuning because multi-step financial analysis is too complex to perform reliably using standard prompts.

items.question: A knowledge manager at a healthcare system is choosing between a RAG architecture and a Claude Project with uploaded documents for a clinical reference assistant. Which TWO characteristics would MOST favour the RAG approach over a Project knowledge upload? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The clinical documents corpus contains 15,000 files — far exceeding what can be curated and maintained in a Project knowledge base.
options.B: The documents are written in highly technical medical language that Project knowledge processing cannot handle correctly.
options.C: Queries will come from multiple users simultaneously, requiring concurrent access that Projects cannot support.
options.D: The corpus is updated weekly as new guidelines are published, and a RAG index can be refreshed automatically while Project knowledge uploads require manual replacement of files.
options.E: The assistant must respond in under two seconds, a latency requirement that RAG cannot meet but Project knowledge can guarantee.

items.question:
A customer success manager at a SaaS platform uses Claude to generate real-time answers to account health questions during live customer calls. The system prompt includes 2,000 tokens of product documentation sent on every API call. Response must be delivered within three seconds. The manager wants to reduce API costs without introducing delivery delay.

The MOST appropriate cost-reduction technique is:

options.A: Prompt caching for the static system prompt — it reduces per-request input cost while maintaining synchronous, real-time response delivery.
options.B: Batch processing — queuing all session queries together and returning responses asynchronously at the end of the call block.
options.C: Fine-tuning the model on the product documentation so the system prompt can be eliminated entirely.
options.D: Switching to a lower-tier model to reduce per-token cost and shortening the system prompt to reduce input volume.

items.question:
A QA lead at a pharmaceutical company is implementing quality assurance for a Claude-powered document review assistant. She is considering two approaches: (1) periodically running a fixed set of representative test documents with defined quality criteria against the system; (2) logging and reviewing a random sample of live production outputs each week.

Approach 1 is BEST characterised as:

options.A: Live output monitoring, which provides real-world signal but cannot detect quality trends over time.
options.B: An evals practice, which establishes a controlled measurement baseline using consistent inputs and defined criteria to reveal changes over time.
options.C: A shadow deployment, which runs the assistant alongside human reviewers and compares outputs for agreement.
options.D: A red-teaming exercise, which tests the system with adversarial or edge-case inputs designed to find failure modes.
